newsitem.title: CANADA: Rogers Comms sees EBITDA growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Rogers Comms sees EBITDA growth in 1997.

text.p: Rogers Communications Inc will enjoy solid growth in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) throughout the remainder of 1997, company executives said on Friday.

"Absolutely, you will see strong (EBITDA) growth. We expect (it) to continue throughout the rest of the year," David Robinson, vice-president of investor relations, told reporters after the company's annual meeting.

Robinson said according to Rogers' business plan, the loss-making cable and wireless telecommunications company expects one quarter in the next three years to show a net profit. He declined to specify which one.
But he said a full year of net profit was not expected in the foreseeable future.
Rogers' EBITDA was C$186 million in the first quarter, a 22.6 percent increase from the C$152 million reported in the prior-year period.
Chief Executive Ted Rogers said the cable unit's growth in the first quarter should be more than equalled in the remainder of 1997.

"My commitment is that as a result of management's focus and the increase in accountability and responsibility of regional of the cable company, that this growth in EBITDA will be more than sustained for the balance of the year," Rogers told the annual meeting.
He said the cable group's first quarter EBITDA rose by 12.7 percent over the same period of 1996.
